data.name: Khatoonah
data.gender_notes: Khatoonah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A noble and graceful woman, often used as a title for women of high status and rank. Derived from the Persian word 'khatoon', meaning 'lady' or 'woman'. The name Khatoonah carries the meaning “Graceful, noblewoman” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Khatoonah usually hope their child will grow to embody graceful, noblewoman and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner grace, elegance, and nobility. Encourages one to be gracious, kind, and respectful to others.
data.etymology: Khatoonah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Graceful, noblewoman.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khatoonah total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Khatoonah carries a sense of elegance, dignity, and grace, which is highly valued in Islamic, Persian, and other Middle Eastern cultures. Khatoonah is a title of respect given to women of high social position, beauty, and refinement. It conveys a sense of nobility, poise, and class, which is deeply embedded in the cultural and social fabric of Islamic societies. Additionally, this name is associated with the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) beloved wife, Khadija, who was a wealthy, successful businesswoman and a respected figure in her own right. Her story is an inspiration to many Muslim women, and the name Khatoonah continues to be used as a source of pride and inspiration.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Khatoonah carries a deep spiritual significance, rooted in the Islamic values of respect, dignity, and compassion. The title implies a sense of reverence and appreciation for women, who are considered delicate, nurturing, and vital contributors to the family and community. In Islamic teachings, women are viewed as essential companions to men, with unique strengths and qualities. The name Khatoonah is a reminder of the importance of honoring and supporting women, as they embody the divine feminine and contribute to the greater good of the world.
